raw_case_text:
A 66-year-old female with a distant 15 pack year smoking history presented to the pulmonary clinic for evaluation of a 4 cm right upper lobe mass found on a CT thorax. She had a dry cough with occasional fatigue and night sweats that began about a year earlier. She denied recent travel, weight loss, hemoptysis, epistaxis, wheezing, joint pain, hematuria, peripheral edema, orthopnea, easy bruising or alopecia. Her vitals and physical exam were within normal limits on room air.
She had been treated as an outpatient for presumed community acquired pneumonia when her symptoms first began. Follow up chest X-ray showed a persistent opacity in the right upper lobe and a CT scan showed a large, spiculated 4 cm right upper lobe mass (Figure 1). It was hypermetabolic with an SUV of 19 on PET CT (Figure 2). Her pulmonary function tests revealed a moderate reduction in diffusion capacity without obstruction or restriction. Her FEV1/FVC ratio was 71%. FVC was 90% of predicted at 2.94 L. FEV1 was 83% of predicted at 2.08 L. Her TLC was 94% of predicted at 4.77 L and vital capacity was 90% of predicted at 2.94 L. Her DLCO was 54% of predicted at 12.8.
She underwent a bronchoscopy and EBUS guided needle aspiration of the mass. Pathology revealed a population of CD10 positive lymphocytes suggestive of follicular lymphoma.
A CT guided biopsy was performed to obtain additional tissue for histological and genetic testing. It surprisingly turned out to be negative for lymphoma but instead showed necrotizing pneumonia. There were areas of necrosis with surrounding fibrosis. Neoplastic cells were not identified (Figures 3 and 4). AFB cultures and fungal cultures were negative. Quantiferon, aspergillus galactomannan, histoplasma, blastomyces and coccidioides antibodies were also negative. ANCA serology including MPO (<9 u/mL) and PR3 (<3.5 u/mL) testing was negative. Rheumatoid factor, C3 and C4 were also negative. Her ANA speckled pattern was 250. Her urinalysis had 3+ protein with a normal protein/creatinine ratio. There were no casts. Her BMP and CBC were within normal limits without eosinophilia.
The patient's cough persisted despite conservative treatment with intranasal steroids, cough suppression, and antihistamines. ENT evaluation with nasopharyngolaryngoscopy (NPL) did not reveal upper airway inflammation or ulceration. A repeat CT scan of the thorax showed that the mass was enlarging.
A video assisted thoracoscopy (VAT) with right upper lobectomy was performed. It revealed a right upper lung mass with multiple adhesions to the pleura. The pathology revealed necrotizing granulomas with eosinophils and giant cells. There were no malignant cells, active vasculitis, or organisms found.
The favored diagnosis was granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 66-year-old female former smoker presented with a 1-year history of dry cough, occasional fatigue, and night sweats and an enlarging 4-cm spiculated right upper lobe lung mass.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed a dry cough, occasional fatigue, and night sweats 1 year prior to presentation and was initially treated as an outpatient for community-acquired pneumonia. Follow-up chest imaging revealed a persistent, enlarging 4-cm spiculated, hypermetabolic (SUV 19) right upper lobe mass that failed to improve with intranasal corticosteroids, antitussives, and antihistamines.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for chronic dry cough, occasional fatigue, and night sweats (1 year); negative for weight loss, hemoptysis, epistaxis, wheezing, arthralgias, hematuria, edema, orthopnea, bruising, alopecia, or recent travel.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs and physical examination were normal on room air; ENT nasopharyngolaryngoscopy showed no upper airway inflammation or mucosal ulceration.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC and BMP were normal without peripheral eosinophilia; urinalysis showed 3+ protein with a normal protein-to-creatinine ratio and no cellular casts. Autoimmune workup showed speckled ANA 1:250 and negative MPO-ANCA (<9 U/mL), PR3-ANCA (<3.5 U/mL), rheumatoid factor, and C3/C4. Pulmonary function tests showed normal spirometry and lung volumes (FEV1/FVC 71%, FVC 2.94 L [90% predicted], FEV1 2.08 L [83%], TLC 4.77 L [94%]) with moderately reduced diffusing capacity (DLCO 12.8 [54% predicted]).
objective.advanced_workup: Chest CT and PET-CT demonstrated an enlarging 4-cm spiculated right upper lobe mass with intense FDG avidity (SUV 19). QuantiFERON-TB, Aspergillus galactomannan antigen, Histoplasma, Blastomyces, and Coccidioides antibodies, and tissue AFB and fungal cultures were all negative. Initial EBUS-TBNA showed CD10+ lymphocytes raising suspicion for follicular lymphoma, whereas CT-guided core biopsy showed only fibrotic necrotizing inflammation without neoplasia. Definitive video-assisted thoracoscopic (VATS) right upper lobectomy demonstrated pleural adhesions and necrotizing granulomas with eosinophils and multinucleated giant cells without malignancy or infectious organisms.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Localized, ANCA-negative pulmonary granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) presenting as a 4-cm hypermetabolic (SUV 19) right upper lobe mass mimicking primary lung malignancy or fungal pneumonia; pulmonary aspergillosis, endemic mycoses, tuberculosis, and follicular lymphoma were excluded by negative Aspergillus galactomannan, fungal/AFB cultures, and VATS right upper lobectomy histopathology confirming necrotizing granulomas with eosinophils and giant cells.
